findings.body:
**Charge the context scan against the triage deadline.**

If `phase()` passes one second of remaining time and the scan takes two seconds, Line 822 still gives the judge a full second. The fallback path then starts a new timer from that stale value. Carry the phase's monotonic deadline through preparation and check it immediately before the driver call. If time remains, pass only that time to the driver. Otherwise, leave the finding pending. ([docs.python.org](https://docs.python.org/3/library/time.html?utm_source=openai))
findings.title: Charge the context scan against the triage deadline.

findings.body:
**Record the provider pause before retaining the worktree.**

If A0 gets rate-limited with fallbacks disabled, a retention failure at Line 520 skips the pause write. If the second retention attempt succeeds, `process()` advances to A1 and can call the same provider immediately. If it fails again, the job can become terminal without recording the pause. Persist the pause first. If retention fails, preserve the checkout and report the failure without advancing the fixer rung.
findings.title: Record the provider pause before retaining the worktree.

findings.body:
**Test shared quarantine before the sibling expires.**

`moved` is created on October 30, 2026, but Line 130 checks it on November 10, 2026. The 24-hour age guard rejects it before `eligible()` reads quarantine history. This assertion would still pass if that history check were removed. Enqueue the sibling just before the sixth failure, then check at the exact 24-hour boundary when cooldown has expired. Verify that an otherwise identical, unquarantined sibling is eligible.
findings.title: Test shared quarantine before the sibling expires.

findings.body:
**Reject explicit selectors in triage preview mode.**

If a caller supplies `--triage-dry-run` with `--job`, `--source-sha`, and `--finding-sha256`, Line 1452 ignores the selected job and can start paid judgments for unrelated findings. Reject the combination before calling `triage_phase()`. Keep standalone preview and standalone explicit repair valid.
findings.title: Reject explicit selectors in triage preview mode.

findings.body:
**Return worker failures in the drain result.**

If the queue is readable before admission but a forked worker cannot reopen it at Line 1011, the child exits with code 1. The coordinator can stop admission, but `drain()` still returns `{"status":"drained"}` with exit code 0. Return an aggregate outcome after reaping all owned children. Preserve the triage report and distinguish worker failures from intentional admission stops.
findings.title: Return worker failures in the drain result.

findings.body:
**Reject an empty recovery selector before dispatch.**

With an enabled runner, `--recover-job ''` bypasses both recovery checks and starts the automatic inbox drain at Line 1516. Detect selector presence with `is not None`, then reject empty or whitespace-only values. Keep a nonempty recovery selector on the single-job path.





Also applies to: 1494-1494
findings.title: Reject an empty recovery selector before dispatch.

findings.body:
**Take `service.lock` before running a triage preview.**

If the drain is judging a pending finding, a concurrent `--triage-dry-run` can read the same pending row and start a second paid judgment with the same job identity and output directory. `dry_run=True` prevents delivery, not judging. Run preview under `service.lock` and return `busy` when another pass owns it.
findings.title: Take `service.lock` before running a triage preview.

findings.body:
**Return a JSON error when explicit selection rejects the pin.**

If `--source-sha` is well formed but differs from the job's pinned SHA, `select_job()` raises `ValueError`. The exception bypasses `write_result()`, so an automated caller gets no JSON. Route selector validation failures to a structured usage result without treating unrelated I/O failures as argument errors. As per coding guidelines, “Every operation invocation writes machine-readable JSON to stdout and human narration to stderr, never mixed.”
findings.title: Return a JSON error when explicit selection rejects the pin.

findings.body:
**Scan `review_diff` before judge dispatch.**

The judge receives the base-to-head `review_diff` without a secret scan. The inbox producer stores the full PR diff in each job (`repair_tick.py:215,229`). The repair path copies it into the judge job (`crq_repair.py:574`) and dispatches that job to the judge (`crq_repair.py:582`). `_dispatch` scans only the source snapshot excerpt (`crq_repair.py:344-350`). It then sends the deep-copied job, including `review_diff`, to the judge driver (`crq_repair.py:340,361-368`). Each judge driver serializes the full job into its prompt (`drivers/cq.py:313`, `drivers/codex.py:191`, `drivers/paseo.py:30`). Removed lines from the base can contain sensitive historical text that is absent from the scanned excerpt. Apply the snapshot policy stated at `crq_repair.py:345` to `review_diff`: scan it before it leaves the machine, and refuse the judge dispatch when the scan rejects it.
findings.title: Scan `reviewdiff` before judge dispatch.

findings.body:
**Require revalidation when the merged-head diff is binary.**

If the published repair adds a line to a text file and a later commit replaces the file with binary contents without changing its mode, Git can report a binary difference with no text hunks. Line 1287 finds no removed lines and accepts the repair as contained. Reconciliation can then record the finding as fixed even though the added line is gone. ([git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitattributes.html?utm_source=openai))

Apply the binary-diff rejection at Line 1274 to `head_patch` as well. Keep the identical-blob shortcut and the existing comparison for text patches.
findings.title: Require revalidation when the merged-head diff is binary.

findings.body:
**Count prepared backfill retry PRs against the cap across ticks.**

Line 74 gives prepared retries a `revalidated-` run ID. Line 691 publishes them on `crq/fix-revalidated-…`, but Line 595 counts only `crq/fix-backfill-…`. With a limit of one, the retry uses the slot on the creation tick and disappears from the count on the next tick, even if its PR is still open.

Use the item’s backfill status to choose the branch prefix. Also count retry branches already published under the old prefix. Keep ordinary fix PRs outside the cap.
findings.title: Count prepared backfill retry PRs against the cap across ticks.

findings.body:
**Lease the journaled target when recovering an open-PR push.**

If Line 714 reads ancestor A, the PR read then sees the prepared target T, and the branch is reset to A before the push, Line 741 accepts A because it is an ancestor of the prepared head. Line 743 then uses A as the lease. Git accepts that lease while the ref is still at A, so the push restores commits the maintainer removed. ([git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-push/2.38.0?utm_source=openai))

For an open PR, use `publication['target']` as the expected ref whenever recovery still needs to push. This preserves retry when the branch is still at T and leaves the already-landed path unchanged.
findings.title: Lease the journaled target when recovering an open-PR push.

findings.body:
**Validate the selected fix PR against the prepared publication.**

The lookups at Lines 761 and 814 filter by branch name, not by commit. If the sole matching PR has an unrelated head, Line 818 still records it as the repair’s fix PR and the next block can enroll it for review. Recovery already rejects that same head mismatch at Line 730. ([cli.github.com](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_list?utm_source=openai))

Request `headRefOid` in both finalization lookups and apply the recovery identity check before recording or enrolling the PR. A singleton at the prepared head should still finalize normally.
findings.title: Validate the selected fix PR against the prepared publication.

findings.body:
**Record a disposition for canonical siblings that have no result when their run fails.**

When a failed run is terminalized, `record_unpublished_siblings` skips every sibling whose `result.json` is missing (`continue` at lines 359-363). It writes no outcome for that sibling. The failed run is no longer `queued`, so the drain does not select the sibling again. The sibling's inbox job stays bound to the dead run, and the digest reports it as orphaned. Require each canonical sibling of a failed run to receive an explicit outcome, as the function's docstring already states: each sibling must get an explicit decision instead of remaining bound to a dead run. The verdict to record is a ledger-contract choice and is not specified here.
findings.title: Record a disposition for canonical siblings that have no result when their run fails.

findings.body:
**Do not return a head older than the checkpoint just observed.**

If this fetch reads A and another validator checkpoints its child B, Line 638 exits the retry loop and returns A. If the remote rolls back to A before publication, the plain push path can append C to A because A→C is a fast-forward. The next fetch rejects C because it does not descend from B. When the checkpoint is strictly newer than the fetched head, retry the fetch within a bound or reject the snapshot. Keep the equal-head case as success. ([git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-update-ref.html?utm_source=openai))
findings.title: Do not return a head older than the checkpoint just observed.

findings.body:
**Return `IntegrityError` for malformed JSON.**

If a retained `.json` file is truncated, `json.loads` raises `JSONDecodeError`. The reader at `apps/crq-python/review_transport.py:293-297` catches `IntegrityError` and `OSError`, so the scan stops before it reaches later valid reviews. Wrap JSON syntax and decoding errors in `IntegrityError` so the reader skips the corrupt record and continues. ([docs.python.org](https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/json.html?utm_source=openai))
findings.title: Return `IntegrityError` for malformed JSON.

findings.body:
**Remove the staging file when an atomic write fails.**

If the file `fsync` or `os.replace` fails, `atomic` leaves the named staging file on disk. A retry creates another file. Repeated failures can consume the space needed to recover, especially when `ArtifactStore.put` is writing report bytes. Record the staging path before the first write and remove it in `finally`. Keep the parent-directory sync after a successful replace. ([docs.python.org](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/tempfile.html?utm_source=openai))
findings.title: Remove the staging file when an atomic write fails.

findings.body:
**Make publish wait only on references that `validate_sequence` checks for non-credited imports.**

For `import-result` records with `result` other than `credited`, `validate_sequence` links only `duplicate_id`. `publish` also waits on `review_id`. The schema permits a non-null `review_id` on an `unverified` record without requiring that review to exist. One such record makes `publish` raise `IntegrityError` before the pending events reach the push step. The record stays in the outbox, so later publish attempts fail the same way and block unrelated pending events.

The required behavior is that the publish dependency set and the sequence check name the same references. Either `publish` stops waiting on `review_id` for non-credited imports, or the schema or `validate` must reject a non-null `review_id` on those records. The choice between these two is not established by the inspected code.
findings.title: Make publish wait only on references that `validatesequence` checks for non-credited imports.

findings.body:
**Bound the decoded line entries per review record.**

The schema does not limit the number of rows in `requested_scope`, `input_scope`, or `reviewed_scope`. Each row expands its intervals into individual line numbers. The only bound is 1,000,000 entries per file, and no bound applies across files or scopes. The record byte cap limits the encoded size, not the decoded entry count. A record of about 1 MiB can therefore expand far beyond any memory budget. For example, ten files in each of three scopes, each with `[1, 100000]`, produce three million entries. All three scope maps are built together before the subset check runs.

Add a limit on the total expanded entries per record, across all rows and all three scopes. Compute the total from the interval bounds before building any set, and reject a record that exceeds it. Choose a limit that keeps valid reviews admissible.
findings.title: Bound the decoded line entries per review record.
